blocks.raw: # Third Party Providers
blocks.text: Third Party Providers

blocks.raw: Information regarding PSD2
blocks.text: Information regarding PSD2

blocks.raw: We allow Third Party Providers (“TPPs”) to:
blocks.text: We allow Third Party Providers (“TPPs”) to:

blocks.raw:
* Get access to an end user’s account information
* Trigger a one-off payment
blocks.text: Get access to an end user’s account informationTrigger a one-off payment

blocks.raw: In order gain access the TPP will need to:
blocks.text: In order gain access the TPP will need to:

blocks.raw:
* Hold a valid eIDAS / OBWAC certificate that Modulr can verify
* Register with Modulr as a TPP
* Get consent from the end user
blocks.text: Hold a valid eIDAS / OBWAC certificate that Modulr can verifyRegister with Modulr as a TPPGet consent from the end user

blocks.raw: ## How does this work?
blocks.text: How does this work?

blocks.raw: Please contact Modulr at [openbanking@modulrfinance.com](openbanking@modulrfinance.com), indicating the certificate you intend to use for mutual TLS. Once we confirm this has been received, you can then register using the endpoint `<baseurl>/register`.  You will need:
blocks.text: Please contact Modulr at openbanking@modulrfinance.com, indicating the certificate you intend to use for mutual TLS. Once we confirm this has been received, you can then register using the endpoint <baseurl>/register.  You will need:

blocks.raw:
* An eIDAS certificate that has been obtained from one of the Qualified Trusted Service Providers. A list of QTSPs can be found here: <https://www.openbankingeurope.eu/qtsps-and-eidas/>
* Or an OBWAC certificate that has been obtained from Open banking UK.
blocks.text: An eIDAS certificate that has been obtained from one of the Qualified Trusted Service Providers. A list of QTSPs can be found here: https://www.openbankingeurope.eu/qtsps-and-eidas/Or an OBWAC certificate that has been obtained from Open banking UK.

### The response will include:

```json
{
    "client_id": "8b7b1bdbcb9242b6bdf249cb6e04ef7c",
```

Then you can list Modulr as an Account Service & Payment Service Provider in your application.
blocks.text: Then you can list Modulr as an Account Service & Payment Service Provider in your application.

blocks.raw: Once a user has selected Modulr in your application you need to use the `<baseurl>/consent` endpoint to get a redirect URL, using this URL to redirect the user to Modulr so they can sign in.
blocks.text: Once a user has selected Modulr in your application you need to use the <baseurl>/consent endpoint to get a redirect URL, using this URL to redirect the user to Modulr so they can sign in.

blocks.raw: The end user will:
blocks.text: The end user will:

blocks.raw:
* Sign in as they usually would for Modulr.
* Consent (or not) to give you access.
* Note: for Payments, the consent can be used only once within one hour. For Account Services, consent duration can be null. There is no limit on maximum consent duration.
blocks.text: Sign in as they usually would for Modulr.Consent (or not) to give you access.Note: for Payments, the consent can be used only once within one hour. For Account Services, consent duration can be null. There is no limit on maximum consent duration.

blocks.raw: They will then be redirected back to you. If they have consented you will be provided with an authorization code.
blocks.text: They will then be redirected back to you. If they have consented you will be provided with an authorization code.

blocks.raw: Using the authorization code you can get an access token via the `<baseurl>/oauth/token` endpoint, which you then use to access the specific action you have gained consent for.
blocks.text: Using the authorization code you can get an access token via the <baseurl>/oauth/token endpoint, which you then use to access the specific action you have gained consent for.

blocks.raw: For account information access you can go back to the token endpoint to get a refreshed access token.
blocks.text: For account information access you can go back to the token endpoint to get a refreshed access token.

blocks.raw: To fetch account information use the endpoint `<baseurl>/accounts`.  The request is a GET with the headers: `X-CLIENT-SSL-CERT`, with your eIDAS/OBWAC certificate and `x-mod-consent-id` with the consent token.
blocks.text: To fetch account information use the endpoint <baseurl>/accounts.  The request is a GET with the headers: X-CLIENT-SSL-CERT, with your eIDAS/OBWAC certificate and x-mod-consent-id with the consent token.

blocks.raw: To make a payment, use the endpoint `<baseurl>/payments`. The request is a POST with the headers: `X-CLIENT-SSL-CERT`, with your eIDAS/OBWAC certificate and `x-mod-consent-id` with the consent token.
blocks.text: To make a payment, use the endpoint <baseurl>/payments. The request is a POST with the headers: X-CLIENT-SSL-CERT, with your eIDAS/OBWAC certificate and x-mod-consent-id with the consent token.
